title: Trump rants about 'TREASONISTS' group that launched lawsuit to stop his ballroom
description_short: Trump rants about 'TREASONISTS' group that launched lawsuit to stop his ballroom
description_medium: Trump has issued a long rant on Truth Social, complaining about a group of 'TREASONISTS' that launched a lawsuit to stop the construction of his White House ballroom. The group, the National Trust for Historic Preservation, has opposed the ballroom's construction and has sued to halt further building at the site.
description_long: On August 15, 2026, Donald Trump posted on Truth Social calling the National Trust for Historic Preservation “TREASONISTS” for suing to stop construction of a White House ballroom. The Trust opposed the project after construction began following the demolition of the East Wing. Trump argued that the ballroom was necessary for national security and presidential safety, and said the lawsuit exposed military secrets. The Independent reported that a federal appeals court had upheld a lower-court ruling that major changes to the White House required congressional authorization. The litigation therefore concerned the president’s authority to undertake substantial construction, while Trump publicly framed the dispute as a security issue. His post attacked the preservation group, but it did not establish that the group had disclosed classified information or committed treason. The article also reported that the administration described a bunker beneath the project and that its cost had risen substantially; those claims are distinct from the court’s ruling. The account documents the public rhetoric and legal dispute without treating Trump’s accusations as findings of fact.
notes: The linked Independent report provides the wording of Trump's post, identifies the National Trust for Historic Preservation, and describes the appellate ruling that Congress must authorize substantial White House changes. The source reports Trump's security claims but does not substantiate that the preservation group disclosed secrets or committed treason.

title: Attorney Matthew Skiba Targets Democrats in Politicized Investigation
description_short: Attorney Matthew Skiba Targets Democrats in Politicized Investigation
description_medium: Attorney Matthew Skiba has been involved in a politicized investigation targeting Democrats, including a Democratic political consulting firm with ties to Judge Juan Merchan, who presided over Trump's hush payment fraud case. The investigation has been criticized as an abuse of power and an attempt to intimidate political opponents.
description_long: An August 2026 Emptywheel post connects Chicago federal prosecutor Matthew Skiba to a subpoena targeting a Democratic political consulting firm with ties to Judge Juan Merchan, who presided over Donald Trump’s New York criminal case. The post identifies prosecutor William Hogan as involved as well and places both men in a separate prosecution of six immigration protesters known as the Broadview Six. That case was withdrawn after Judge April Perry raised concerns about prosecutors’ conduct before a grand jury. Emptywheel argues that the subpoena investigation was politically retaliatory and links it to Merchan’s family, but the post’s interpretation is not an official finding. The supplied record does not name the consulting firm, reproduce the subpoena, explain which records were sought, or provide responses from the prosecutors or U.S. attorney. Those details are necessary to evaluate the connection and the allegation of retaliation. The available source supports a report of the investigation and a commentator’s criticism, not a definitive finding that Skiba targeted Democrats to punish a judge.
notes: The linked Emptywheel post is commentary and makes the retaliation claim as an interpretation. It identifies a subpoena and the Broadview Six case but the supplied packet does not name the consulting firm, provide the subpoena or responses from the prosecutors, or establish a connection to Merchan's family. Those records are needed to verify the allegation.
